title: Construction, Maintenance and Minor Works Framework
description:
The proposed framework is intended to provide the Council with access to suitably experienced and competent contractors capable of delivering a range of planned, reactive and project-based works across the Council estate. The scope will include, but is not limited to, general building works, minor civil works, repair and maintenance activities, small-scale refurbishment, enabling works and associated construction-related services.
The proposed framework will offer access to a range of construction and minor works trades and disciplines, including painting and decorating, plastering, plumbing, Gas Safe engineering, joinery, drywall and ceilings, skilled labour, general labouring, fence erection, glazing, bricklaying and stonemasonry, tiling, welding and roofing, playpark installations.
The estimated total value of the Framework over its term is £1,500,000. This estimate is provided for transparency and planning purposes only and does not constitute a guarantee of volume of work or number of call-off contracts to be awarded under the Framework.
The framework will be used exclusively for works and contractors/individuals located within the borough area of Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council.
It is intended to support the efficient, compliant and timely delivery of Council requirements across the Borough whilst providing support to local firms through direct procurement and ensuring that works are procured and delivered in a manner that meets Council's operational needs, statutory responsibilities and commitment to transparency in public procurement.
The framework is not intended to confer exclusivity on any single supplier, and any subsequent call-off arrangements will be managed in accordance with the terms of the Framework and the applicable requirements of the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024.
Council considers that the framework is particularly suitable for small and medium-sized enterprises. The nature, scale and geographic focus of the works are expected to provide opportunities for local and regional contractors, including SMEs, to participate as subcontractors.

title: BaDC-1727 Retford Buttermarket Food Hall Operator Opportunity
description:
Bassetlaw District Council (the Council) wishes to invite tenders to appoint a suitably experienced operator to occupy and operate an indoor street food market within the Retford Town Hall's Buttermarket.
The operator will be responsible for all aspects of delivery, vendor management and commercial performance, in return for the right to trade from the premises and an opportunity to influence the final design and fit-out of the space.
The Council's objectives in appointing an operator are to:
•	Animate and activate Retford town centre
•	Support independent and start-up food businesses
•	Provide a high-quality, diverse and affordable food offer
•	Increase footfall and dwell time
•	Support the evening and weekend economy
•	Deliver social and economic value for the local area
The Buttermarket is anticipated to be available to the operator for commercial operation from Winter 2026/Spring 2027 subject to detailed design agreement and construction programme. The Council envisions the successful provider from this tender to join as a partner through this design process. This interim period for design and Council construction will ensure the final installation is fit for purpose and encourages optimal commercial operation for the appointed end user.
Location
Located on the Market Square, Retford Town Hall is well positioned to amplify the offerings of the town, however, the site is currently greatly underutilised, and its facilities require significant modernisation. The Buttermarket is the ground floor premise of the wider Retford Town Hall with its own level and independent access along the Town Hall Yard and direct access to the Market Square. There is ample area (~260m2) to enhance this space to provide a series of catering focused opportunities while also creating an inclusive communal space, designed to host events that appeal across all age groups.
According to a recent market summary of Retford undertaken by CACI, the town boasts a sizable catchment area with a total market potential of £122.1 million. Additionally, Retford enjoys a high catchment market share of 16%, indicating a strong local spend for retailers and food businesses opening in the town centre. The total market potential for catering alone is £30.1 million.
The overall spend remains below the regional average, indicating a need for Retford to build up a critical mass of retail and leisure offer to increase its attractiveness. Annual household spent on catering is £2,060 which is 5% lower than the East Midlands average and spend on alcohol on premises is 10% below the regional average demonstrating there is available spend for these types of offers not currently being realised in Retford.
Mandatory Site Visit
Attendance at a mandatory supervised site visit is a condition of participation in this procurement process.
The site visit will take place at: Buttermarket, Retford Town Hall, DN22 6DE
Site visits will be conducted on 16th November 2026.
Bidders must register in advance to attend the site visit. Instructions for registering and arranging attendance are set out in Section 7.2 of this document.
Only bidders who have successfully registered and attended a site visit in accordance with these instructions will be eligible to submit a tender.
Please note: The Council reserves the right to eliminate bids from the procurement process (without evaluation), that are received from any potential supplier that has not attended a site visit.
Full details of the opportunity and the Council's requirements are set out in the tender documents.
Term
The Council would optimally seek a 5-year lease with a break clause at Year 3 and the opportunity to extend a further 5 years at year 5 (3+2+5 year agreement).
Procurement Procedure
This is a competitive flexible procedure. Initial tenders will be scored based on price quality as out lined in document 1.
Up to the top 3 bidders will then be invited to a presentation stage which will be scored out of 100 (the scoring for which is in appendix 5).
The final tender score will be calculated based on the weightings of the price and quality score from the previous round making up  90% of score and the presentation will form the remaining 10%.

title: External Cyclical Maintenance
description:
The works include, but are not limited to, the provision of surveys and design services, consultation with customers including design development, and the scheduling and programming of all elements of the service. The works also encompass the installation, construction, repair, maintenance, renewal, reinstatement, replacement and/or improvement of structural components, roof coverings, fascias, bargeboards, soffits, rainwater goods, windows, external doors, fire safety measures, internal doors and frames, retrofit and energy efficiency measures, play areas, external paving, fencing and other environmental components, together with any additional works identified by the Client.
Window repairs or replacements undertaken as part of External Cyclical Maintenance Planned Schemes will generally involve a limited number of windows at an individual property. It is not anticipated that such schemes will require the replacement of a significant number of windows or the complete replacement of all windows within a property.
The works also include cyclical redecoration, comprising the redecoration of existing painted or decorated surfaces, including windows, doors, fascias, rainwater and sanitary pipework, walls, soffits to external elevations, and common areas including communal rooms. Cyclical redecoration may also extend to bin stores, garages, cycle sheds, fencing, railings, screens, gates and similar features located within boundaries, paths, drives, communal areas, staircases, access decks and balconies.
Cyclical redecoration shall be deemed to include the cleaning, where specified, of external surfaces of components and products such as windows, doors, soffits, fascias, cladding and other similar elements encountered during the works.
The works further include pre-decoration repairs, comprising the repair, maintenance, renewal, reinstatement or replacement of previously decorated elements and components where such works are required prior to cyclical redecoration. This includes the inspection, repair and adjustment of hinges, locking mechanisms, handles and security devices associated with UPVC windows and external or communal doors.
The works also include the identification, surveying, management, removal and disposal of asbestos-containing materials where these are discovered during the course of the works

title: Invitation to Tender for the Management of the Cleaning Services at Greenhead College
description:
Aims of the Service and Tender
The key aims of the tender are to:
	Provide a high standard of cleaning 
	Deliver the cleaning services with consistency - good quality assurance systems in place
	Good communication at local and operations manager level with the College - two-way communication
	Daily interaction with the College representative at each site
	Develop an effective method of handing over any special needs and comments on a daily basis
	A Contractor that adopts a flexible and proactive approach to all College activities. 
	Cleaners to work the hours that best suit the needs of the College and maximise the work completed
	A Contractor that operates using the optimum level of staffing. 
	Training and development of the teams at the College
This does not imply that this is not happening now - these are the aims of the contract.
The College work to provide the students with the very best experiences they can. The quality of the environment in which they all work together is very important to us. The cleanliness and good order of the classrooms, corridors, social and dining spaces and other areas of the College impacts upon the teaching and learning that goes within the College. The College expectations are high, and they are looking for a cleaning contractor who has the same aims and aspirations as we do. They do seek value for money but that does not mean they will choose the cheapest quote possible. They are seeking a partner who will be willing to undertake extra work and be flexible in approach when dealing with certain key events in our year.
Suppliers of cleaning services to all College buildings should ensure the following criteria are met: 
•	All site based and visiting staff are Enhanced DBS checked 
•	All staff wear College ID badges and company branded workwear 
•	Quality assurance schedule to be carried out by the supplier daily 
•	Any signs of vandalism or graffiti to be reported to College designated personnel daily 
•	Cleaning fluids should be compliant with relevant public services specifications 
•	All cleaning equipment and chemicals should be stored in the designated cupboards and locked at all times 
•	Supplier to provide own equipment & cleaning products 
•	Report any maintenance issues identified during cleaning to the premises team so they can be rectified as soon as possible. 
•	Supervisors should be non-working to ensure the team are monitored and lone working is reduced to an absolute minimum. 
•	Deep cleans will be by agreement in all College holidays, excepting for Christmas closure (2 weeks)
